title: The Final page of the book
subtitle: 决策选择 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）
meta: 主题语境：决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）　|　核心词汇：final　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 final 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the shopkeeper wrote of ① a final page of the book in the account, and everybody in the shop said at once that it was ② so final that nobody in the shop would go near it. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the shopkeeper, who never explained anything, had done it in the rain and gone home; it was the final ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the final page of the book that anybody there had ever seen, or so the account for July 1960 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too final to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the buyer who had come to help; the final ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the scale at the far counter, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a final word from the office, and said that no buyer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as final as the word from the office they had once had in the old shop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was final or not, and he said so.

By 1973 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the account. What the line asked for was ⑦ something final, and nothing besides. The buyer from the next shop called the whole plan ⑧ quite final; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the account kept the names of the final ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1976, without complaint, she wrote of another final page of the book in the same account, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ no less final than anybody had expected. ⑩ The final word from the office that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1978, was the one she could never quite name; the final ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 最后（前置定语 a final page of the book：1966 年掌柜在账本里记下的那件最后的一页）
B. adj. 最后／最终（两处加强说法：so final that … 与 no less final than …）
C. adj. 最后／最终（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 最后（表语 too final to do：母亲觉得它太最后，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 最终（前置定语 a final word from the office：叔叔把整件事称作一桩最终的答复）
F. adj. 最终（同级比较 as final as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩办公室的最终答复相比）
G. adj. 最终（后置定语 something final：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 最终（受程度副词修饰 quite final：那位买主的评价）

items.q: a final page of the book
the final page of the book that
a final word from the office
The final word from the office that

answers.why: final 意为“最后”，1966 年掌柜在账本里记下的是“一件最后的一页”，此处作前置定语 a final page of the book。
final 意为“最后”，此处用 so final that 结构，说它最后到铺子里没人敢靠近。
final 意为“最后”，账本上 七月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的最后书的最后一页，等于最高级的说法。
final 意为“最后”，母亲认为这件东西“太最后了，谁也用不上”，too final to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
final 意为“最终”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩最终的答复”，此处作前置定语 a final word from the office。
final 意为“最终”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩办公室的最终答复一样最终”，同级比较用 as final as。
final 意为“最终”，账本上那半行字要的是“最终的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something final。
final 意为“最终”，邻铺子来的那位买主认为这套计划“相当最终”，quite 修饰原级 final。
final 意为“最终”，no less final than 表示“其最终不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之最终不亚于任何人的预料。
final 意为“最终”，母亲 1978 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的最终答复”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1966 年，掌柜在账本里记下了一件最后的一页。（a final page of the book）
它最后到铺子里没有一个人敢靠近。（so final that …）
母亲觉得它太最后，谁也用不上。（too final to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩最终的答复。（a final word from the office）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩办公室的最终答复一样最终。（as final as …）
到了 1973 年，账本上只剩半行字：要的是一件最终的东西。（something final）
answers: In 1966 the shopkeeper wrote of a final page of the book in the account.
It was so final that nobody in the shop would go near it.
My mother thought it too final to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a final word from the office.
He said nobody would call it as final as the word from the office they had once had.
By 1973 the account asked for nothing but something final.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 final 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1966 the shopkeeper wrote of a final page of the book in the account, and nobody forgot it.
It was the final page of the book that anybody there had ever seen, or so the account says.
My mother thought it too final to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a final word from the office, and nobody argued with him.
The buyer from the next shop called the plan quite final, and everybody laughed.
The final ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
